questions.stem: What does 「しゅみは何ですか。」 ask?
options: What are your interests or hobbies?
What is your favourite food?
What job do you want to have in the future?
What did you do on the weekend?
questions.explanation: 「しゅみ」 means hobby or interest, so this asks what you like to do in your free time. A future career would be asked with 「しょうらい」.

questions.stem: Which verb goes with 「ピアノ」 in 'to play the piano'?
options: たたく
ひく
する
ふく
questions.explanation: Keyboard and stringed instruments take 「ひく」: 「ピアノをひく」, 「ギターをひく」. 「ふく」 is for wind instruments such as the flute, and 「たたく」 is for drums.

questions.stem: Which verb completes 「毎週土曜日にサッカーを___。」 ('I play soccer every Saturday')?
options: します
ひきます
あそびます
やすみます
questions.explanation: Most ball sports take 「する」: 「サッカーをする」, 「テニスをする」. 「ひく」 is for instruments, and 「あそぶ」 means to play in the sense of having fun, not to play a sport.

questions.stem: What does 「私のしゅみはえいがを見ることと、えをかくことです。」 tell you?
options: She wants to make films and paint later
She watched a film and then drew a picture today
She likes films but does not like drawing
Her interests are watching films and drawing
questions.explanation: 「〜ことと、〜ことです」 lists two activities as her hobbies, using 「こと」 to turn the verbs into nouns. Nothing in the sentence refers to today or to future plans.

questions.stem: Your friend asks 「いっしょにえいがを見に行きませんか。」 What is she doing?
options: Telling you she can't go to the film
Asking you to lend her a film
Inviting you to go to a film with her
Asking whether you have seen the film
questions.explanation: ます base + 「ませんか」 is a polite invitation, and 「見に行く」 means to go to see. Although it is negative in form, it is not a refusal.

questions.stem: What does 「しあいにかちました。」 mean?
options: We won the match.
We lost the match.
We watched the match.
We drew the match.
questions.explanation: 「しあい」 is a match or game and 「かつ」 means to win. Losing is 「まける」, the verb students most often confuse it with.

questions.stem: 「バスケットボールのれんしゅうは、毎週火曜日と木曜日の朝です。」 When is basketball practice?
options: Tuesday and Thursday mornings
Tuesday and Friday mornings
Wednesday and Thursday mornings
Tuesday and Thursday evenings
questions.explanation: 「火曜日」 is Tuesday, 「木曜日」 is Thursday and 「朝」 is morning. 「金曜日」 (Friday) is easily mixed up with 「木曜日」.

questions.stem: 「チームのみんなとれんしゅうするのは楽しいですが、朝はやくおきなければならないのはたいへんです。」 How does the writer feel?
options: She enjoys training but wants to leave the team soon
She finds both the training and the early starts easy
She enjoys training with the team but finds the early starts hard
She finds training with the team hard but enjoys the early starts
questions.explanation: The first clause says practising with the team is fun, and 「が」 introduces the contrast: having to get up early is hard. The second option swaps the two halves.

questions.stem: What does 「私はシドニーのチームをおうえんしています。」 mean?
options: I coach a team in Sydney.
I moved to a Sydney team.
I support a Sydney team.
I play for a Sydney team.
questions.explanation: 「おうえんする」 means to cheer for or support a team. Playing for a team would be 「チームに入っている」 or 「チームでプレーしている」.

questions.stem: 「オーストラリアでは、クリケットは夏に、フットボールは冬にすることが多いです。」 What does the sentence say?
options: In Australia both cricket and football are mostly played in winter
In Australia cricket is mostly a winter sport and football a summer one
In Australia more people play cricket than play football
In Australia cricket is mostly a summer sport and football a winter one
questions.explanation: 「クリケットは夏に、フットボールは冬に」 pairs each sport with its season, and 「〜ことが多い」 means it is usually so. The sentence does not compare how many people play.

questions.stem: What does 「けんこうにいい」 mean?
options: bad for your health
very healthy already
about health
good for your health
questions.explanation: 「けんこう」 is health and 「〜にいい」 means good for, so 「やさいはけんこうにいい」 means vegetables are good for your health. 'Bad for your health' would be 「けんこうにわるい」.

questions.stem: What advice does 「あまいものを食べすぎないほうがいいですよ。」 give?
options: You should eat more sweet things every day.
You must not eat any sweet things at all.
You can eat sweet things if you exercise.
You had better not eat too many sweet things.
questions.explanation: 「食べすぎない」 is 'not eat too much' and ない form + 「ほうがいい」 gives advice not to do something. It warns against too many sweets rather than banning them, which would be 「〜てはいけません」.

questions.stem: What does 「うんどうぶそく」 mean?
options: Being too tired to exercise
Not getting enough sleep
Not getting enough exercise
Getting too much exercise
questions.explanation: 「うんどう」 is exercise and 「ぶそく」 means a shortage, so the word means a lack of exercise. A lack of sleep is 「ねぶそく」.

questions.stem: 「さいきん、うんどうぶそくなので、毎朝三十分ジョギングすることにしました。」 What has the writer done?
options: Jogged for thirty minutes this morning
Been told by a doctor to jog for thirty minutes a day
Stopped jogging because she was tired
Decided to jog for thirty minutes every morning
questions.explanation: 「ことにしました」 shows a decision the writer made herself, giving lack of exercise as the reason. Being told to do it by someone else would be 「〜ように言われました」 or 「ことになりました」.

questions.stem: What does 「朝ご飯を食べないで学校に行くのは、体によくないです。」 mean?
options: Going to school without breakfast is bad for you.
Eating breakfast at school is bad for your body.
Going to school after breakfast is good for you.
Skipping school to eat breakfast is bad.
questions.explanation: 「食べないで」 means 'without eating', and 「体によくない」 means not good for your body. The sentence is about skipping breakfast, not about where breakfast is eaten.

questions.stem: What does 「かぜをひきました。」 mean?
options: The wind is strong.
I pulled a muscle.
I have caught a cold.
I have broken my arm.
questions.explanation: 「かぜをひく」 is the set phrase for catching a cold. 「かぜ」 can also mean wind, but with 「ひく」 it means a cold.

questions.stem: A doctor says 「二、三日、学校を休んで、よくねてください。」 What should you do?
options: Stay home from school for a few days and get plenty of sleep
Go to school for two or three days, then rest
Sleep for two or three hours in the sick bay at school each day
Take two or three days of medicine, then return
questions.explanation: 「二、三日」 means two or three days, 「学校を休んで」 means taking time off school, and 「よくねて」 means sleep well. Nothing is said about medicine or going to school.

questions.stem: How is 「旅行」 read?
options: たびこう
りょいき
りょこう
りょうこう
questions.explanation: 「旅行」 (travel, a trip) is 「りょこう」, with a short 「りょ」. 「りょうこう」 lengthens the first vowel, a common slip.

questions.stem: What does 「休みの日は、たいてい何をしますか。」 ask?
options: Which day of the week is your day off?
Do you want to take a day off next week?
What do you usually do on your days off?
What did you do on your last day off?
questions.explanation: 「たいてい」 means usually, and the non-past 「しますか」 asks about habit. A question about one past day off would use 「しましたか」.

questions.stem: 「冬休みに、メルボルンのおばの家にとまりました。毎日町を歩いたり、店で買い物をしたりしました。天気はよくなかったけど、楽しかったです。」 What does the writer say?
options: The weather wasn't good, but she enjoyed her stay
The weather was good, so she enjoyed her stay
She stayed in a hotel and shopped every day
Her aunt came to stay with her family in winter
questions.explanation: 「天気はよくなかったけど、楽しかったです」 says the weather was poor but she had a good time. She stayed at her aunt's house (「おばの家にとまりました」), not in a hotel.

questions.stem: Which sentence asks whether someone has ever been to the Great Barrier Reef?
options: 「グレートバリアリーフに行ったことがありますか。」
「グレートバリアリーフに行くことがありますか。」
「グレートバリアリーフに行きたいですか。」
「グレートバリアリーフに行くつもりですか。」
questions.explanation: Past た form + 「ことがありますか」 asks about experience. The non-past 「行くことがありますか」 asks whether you sometimes go, and 「つもり」 asks about intention.

questions.stem: What does 「夏休みに家族と海の近くでキャンプをしました。」 mean?
options: In the summer holidays my family will camp near the sea.
In the summer holidays I camped by a lake with my family.
In the summer holidays I camped near the beach with my family.
In the summer holidays I went to the beach with my friends.
questions.explanation: 「海の近くで」 means near the sea or beach, and the past 「しました」 places it in the past. The third option changes the tense to the future.

questions.stem: What does 「私の家は駅から近いです。」 mean?
options: My house is close to the station.
My house is far from the station.
My house is in front of the station.
My house is a station.
questions.explanation: 「〜から近い」 means close to a place, here the station. 'Far from' would be 「〜から とおい」.

questions.stem: In 「私のへやは二かいにあります。」, where is the room in Australian terms?
options: On the ground floor, at street level, by the door
Two floors up, above the first floor
In the second room along the hall
Upstairs, on the first floor above the ground floor
questions.explanation: Japanese counts the ground floor as 「一かい」, so 「二かい」 is the first floor up, which Australians call the first floor. Reading it as two floors up is the usual mistake.

questions.stem: What does 「家のとなりに公園があります。」 mean?
options: There is a park behind my house.
There is a park inside my house.
There is a park next to my house.
There is a park in front of my house.
questions.explanation: 「となり」 means next door or beside. In front of is 「前」 and behind is 「うしろ」.

questions.stem: 「私の家にはにわがありませんが、近くに大きい公園があります。」 What does the writer say?
options: There's a small garden and no park in the area
There's no garden, but there's a big park nearby
There's a big garden and a park nearby
There's no park nearby, but the garden is big
questions.explanation: 「にわがありません」 says there is no garden, and 「が」 introduces the contrast: a big park nearby. The third option reverses the two facts.

questions.stem: What does 「本だなはつくえの右にあります。」 mean?
options: The bookshelf is to the left of the desk.
The bookshelf is on top of the desk.
The bookshelf is to the right of the desk.
The desk is to the right of the bookshelf.
questions.explanation: In 「〜は〜の右にあります」, the thing marked by 「は」 is to the right of the one before 「の」. Swapping the two nouns is the common slip with location phrases.

questions.stem: Which form completes 「私はシドニーに___。」 ('I live in Sydney')?
options: 住みました
住んでいました
住んでいます
住みます
questions.explanation: Where you live now is expressed with 「住んでいる」, the ongoing state. 「住みます」 means 'will live', and 「住んでいました」 means you lived there in the past.

questions.stem: How is 「近所」 read?
options: きんしょ
ちかじょ
きんじょ
ちかしょ
questions.explanation: 「近所」 (the neighbourhood) uses on-readings: 「きん」 + 「じょ」. 「ちかしょ」 mixes in the kun-reading of 「近い」.

questions.stem: 「私の町はしずかで住みやすいですが、店が少なくて、ちょっとふべんです。」 What does the writer think of the town?
options: It is quiet, and very convenient for shopping
It is quiet and easy to live in, but a bit inconvenient
It is lively and convenient, with many shops
It is noisy, but it has plenty of shops
questions.explanation: 「しずかで住みやすい」 gives the good points, and after 「が」, 「店が少なくて、ちょっとふべん」 says few shops make it inconvenient. 「ふべん」 is the opposite of 「べんり」.

questions.stem: What is 「いなか」?
options: A suburb by the sea
The countryside
The city centre
A shopping centre
questions.explanation: 「いなか」 means the countryside, or a rural home town. The city centre is 「町の中心」 or 「都心」.

questions.stem: 「えき前に大きいスーパーがあって、買い物にべんりです。」 Why is the area convenient?
options: The station is right next to a very big park
There are many small shops near the school
The supermarket delivers to every house
There is a big supermarket in front of the station
questions.explanation: 「えき前」 means in front of the station, and 「買い物にべんりです」 means handy for shopping. The sentence mentions no park, school or delivery.

questions.stem: What does 「キャンベラはオーストラリアのしゅとです。」 mean?
options: Canberra is the largest city in Australia.
Canberra is a famous beach in Australia.
Canberra is the oldest city in Australia.
Canberra is the capital of Australia.
questions.explanation: 「しゅと」 means capital city. Sydney is the largest city, which is why 'largest' tempts.

questions.stem: 「グレートバリアリーフは、せかいで一番大きいさんごしょうです。」 What does the sentence say?
options: It is the largest coral reef system in the world
It is the oldest coral reef in the world
It is the most beautiful beach in the world
It is the largest island in the whole world
questions.explanation: 「せかいで一番大きい」 means the largest in the world, and 「さんごしょう」 is a coral reef. The sentence makes no claim about age or beauty.

questions.stem: 「シドニーのオペラハウスは、せかいいさんです。」 What is the Opera House called here?
options: A famous shopping centre
The tallest building in Australia
A World Heritage site
The oldest building in Sydney
questions.explanation: 「せかいいさん」 means World Heritage, and the Sydney Opera House was added to the World Heritage List in 2007. The sentence does not claim it is old or tall.

questions.stem: 「オーストラリアに来たら、ぜひブルーマウンテンズに行ってください。シドニーから電車で二時間ぐらいで行けます。」 What does the writer say?
options: The Blue Mountains train runs only twice a day from Sydney
You can reach the Blue Mountains from Sydney by train in about two hours
The Blue Mountains are two hours by car from Sydney's airport
You should visit Sydney first, then take a two-hour flight
questions.explanation: 「シドニーから電車で」 means by train from Sydney, and 「二時間ぐらいで行けます」 means you can get there in about two hours, using the potential 「行ける」. 「二時間」 is a length of time, not twice a day.
